name: pgrubic
description: PostgreSQL linter and formatter for schema migrations and design best practices.

documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: pgrubic pgrubic is a PostgreSQL linter and formatter for schema migrations and design best practices.

documents.title: Features
documents.text: - Over 100+ rules - Automatic violation correction (e.g., automatically add concurrently to index create statements) - River style code formatting for DML statements - Almost identical styling with pg dump for DDL statements - Python 3.12+ compatibility - Automatic caching to avoid reformatting unchanged files - Violations suppression, statement level, and file level - Can be used as a library in your own Python projects, not just as a CLI tool

documents.title: via Web Browser
documents.text: Lint, format, and fix your migrations directly in your browser, no installation required: Try it online

documents.title: Configuration
documents.text: pgrubic can be configured via the [ pgrubic.toml ] file in either the current directory, up to the root directory or the path set by the PGRUBIC CONFIG PATH environment variable. Config values can also be overridden using the --config command-line argument, which accepts a TOML = pair and may be repeated, e.g. --config "lint.target-postgres-version = 17" . documents.title: Rules
documents.text: There are 100+ rules. All rules are enabled by default. For a complete list, see rules.

documents.title: Contributing
documents.text: We welcome and greatly appreciate contributions. If you would like to contribute, please see the contributing guidelines.

documents.title: Support
documents.text: Encountering issues? Take a look at the existing GitHub issues, and don't hesitate to open a new one.

documents.title: Acknowledgments
documents.text: pgrubic is inspired by a number of similar tools such as Strong Migrations, squabble, squawk, pgextwlist, Don't Do This and schemalint. pgrubic is built upon the shoulders of: - pglast - Python bindings to libpg query - libpg query - PostgreSQL parser outside of the server environment
